svg.title: Three research decisions: from shared energy to useful observations
svg.desc: A conceptual progression through resource, information and sensing decisions. Dynamic-K adapts the maximum number of concurrent donors. DA-IES-S values new information and safeguards payer reserves. Sentinel-assisted sensing wakes neighbours after a local change; a separate trace-based extension uses bounded re-alerts as an event moves. In each study the ten-node hardware-in-the-loop testbed answers a different question: live donor control under delivered reports, offline policy replay on common radio traffic, or physical acknowledgements of local wake commands.
svg.text: From shared energy to useful observations

g.text: How many donors should serve one receiver?
Dynamic-K adjusts the limit on simultaneous donors as reserves change.
Live control: the controller adapts the limit live, using the reports that arrive.
Which energy reports could change the next transfer?
DA-IES-S weighs a report’s value against its cost and protects payer reserves.
Matched replay: alternative policies are replayed on the same captured radio traffic.
Where should sensors wake or look again?
Sentinel-assisted sampling wakes neighbours when a local signal changes.
A separate trace study tests bounded re-alerts as an event spreads.
Wake verification: radio acknowledgements show which local wake commands arrive.
